title: Qualitative exploration of sociocultural determinants of health inequities of Dalit population in Dhaka City, Bangladesh
relevance: BMJ Open mixed qualitative study in two Dalit/sweeper colonies in Dhaka found interactions with non-Dalits affected by an intertwined caste-occupation identity and impurity/hygiene stigma.
limitations: Does not isolate municipal occupation from Dalit ancestry/caste or prove the tea-service event; a civic tea refusal attributed purely to occupation is a hypothesis.

title: Occupational health and safety status of waste and sanitation workers: A qualitative exploration during the COVID-19 pandemic across Bangladesh
relevance: PLOS Water nationwide field interviews include one Coxs Bazar municipal supervisor describing waste workers as uneducated and unskilled; report also documents gaps in occupational training.
limitations: Supervisor cited occupational skills, not neutral form checking despite equal training; evidence may reflect observed real differences in job-specific training.

title: Poverty and stigma in urban Bangladesh: conceptual contributions and empirical explorations
relevance: Policy Press poverty-stigma article reports a female domestic worker in Dhaka told she could not use her workplace building lift, and interprets occupation as a moderator of exclusion.
limitations: Embedded in poverty study, one qualitative report, not proof of occupation-only causality; Q03 V1 currently has competing written-permission answer.

title: Sufferings in silence: Violence against female workers in the ready-made garment industry in Bangladesh: A qualitative exploration
publisher: Akhter et al., Womens Health / SAGE
relevance: 2019 four-factory qualitative study finds supervisors called female garment workers disobedient and uncooperative, alongside reports of workplace violence and suppression.
limitations: Workplace supervisors judging female employees does not demonstrate unrelated municipal-hearing hostility; gender and power are confounders.

title: Why Bangladeshi nurses avoid 'nursing': social and structural factors on hospital wards in Bangladesh
publisher: Social Science & Medicine; Qualitative Health Research
relevance: Hadley et al. (2007) six-hospital interviews document nursing associated with improper female conduct because of night duty, strangers and intimate care; Zaman (2009) documents negative images of nurses.
limitations: Historical attitudes and gender-specific setting cannot be assumed prevalent today or across all nurse genders; moral character of an individual is never a fact derived from occupation.

title: Ladies without lamps: nurses in Bangladesh
relevance: Zaman (2009) nurses negative images; abstract accessible via search indexed
limitations: Historical attitudes and gender-specific setting cannot be assumed prevalent today or across all nurse genders; moral character of an individual is never a fact derived from occupation.

title: Perception regarding health and barriers to seeking healthcare services among rural rickshaw pullers in Bangladesh: A qualitative exploration
relevance: 2022 interviews with 20 rural rickshaw pullers mention long healthcare waits, social class inequality, costs and experiences of not being valued.
limitations: Poverty, rural access, triage, ability to pay may shape delays; not proof that equal-paying people with identical clinical symptoms receive differential registration due solely to occupation.

title: The Process of Social Exclusion of Tea Garden Workers: A Study on Sylhet City Corporation, Bangladesh
publisher: Asian Journal of Humanity, Art and Literature; UK FCDO
relevance: 2018 field survey/interviews in Sylhet indicate tea-garden workers face political/social exclusion; UK FCDO 2018 report identifies severe marginalisation with ancestry and migration history.
limitations: Occupation is entangled with ethnicity/ancestry and residential isolation; evidence does not prove individual clerks omit identical community submissions based on employment alone.

title: Modern slavery within the tea industry in Bangladesh
relevance: FCDO review: workers descended mostly from India and marginalised; shows ancestry confound
limitations: Occupation is entangled with ethnicity/ancestry and residential isolation; evidence does not prove individual clerks omit identical community submissions based on employment alone.

title: Vulnerability mapping to help sex workers in Bangladesh and Myanmar
relevance: UNAIDS January 2021 article reports stigma and discrimination as barriers to alternative employment among Bangladeshi sex workers; 2025 published analysis summarizes wider community exclusion.
limitations: UNAIDS captures self-reports, not an experiment on public library volunteer placement; gender/religion and legal/social safeguards can confound.

title: Socio-cultural challenges and mental health needs of female sex workers in Bangladesh: a call for culturally sensitive interventions
relevance: 2025 Bangladesh-focused review reports exclusion from community/religious life; not a primary experiment
limitations: UNAIDS captures self-reports, not an experiment on public library volunteer placement; gender/religion and legal/social safeguards can confound.

title: Investigating the Working Environment and the Hindrance Faced by Street Hawkers in Bangladesh: An Empirical investigation in Dhaka City
publisher: Journal of Economics and Sustainable Development; Journal of Contemporary Asia
relevance: 2019 Dhaka study reports surveyed support for street-hawker eviction and hostile working conditions; Lata 2021 describes stigmatization, eviction and extortion of urban informal vendors.
limitations: Eviction preferences may reflect legitimate pavement access concerns; not evidence hawkers intrinsically disrupt unrelated queue duties.

title: To Whom Does the City Belong? Obstacles to Right to the City for the Urban Poor in Bangladesh
relevance: Lutfun Nahar Lata (2021) describes stigmatization and exclusion of Dhaka informal vendors
limitations: Eviction preferences may reflect legitimate pavement access concerns; not evidence hawkers intrinsically disrupt unrelated queue duties.

title: Peasants’ Viewpoint on Bringing the Next Generation into Agriculture: Insights from Bangladesh
publisher: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
relevance: Small Bangladesh village focus groups describe farming as unattractive, unprofitable and "unskilled" to some surveyed young people.
limitations: No finding about farmers being incapable with tablets, SMS, or digital attendance; no valid inferential link to the specific digital incompetence mechanism.
